rounds.text: Likhami Consulting Ltd is demonstrating tangible operational improvement through margin expansion, evidenced by the TTM operating margin rising to 41% from 35% three years prior, representing a solid six percentage point increase [E30]. Furthermore, the market capitalization stands at a substantial ₹ 297 Cr [E3], reflecting a sizeable enterprise base for these strengthening core margins. Conceded: the company carries a high price-to-earnings multiple of 929x [E1] and a price-to-book ratio of 8.47x [E2]. Conceded: the return on equity remains low at 0.66% against a sector benchmark of 4.99% [E9], alongside a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4]. Finally, the stock trades near the lower end of its range at 18% of its 52-week span [E5].

Likhami Consulting Ltd trades at an extraordinary valuation that is completely disconnected from its underlying profitability, evidenced by a staggering P/E ratio of 929x [E1] or 934.06x against a sector benchmark of just 18.13x [E6]. This massive multiple requires investors to pay a ₹ 297 Cr market capitalisation [E3] for a business that generates virtually no meaningful returns for shareholders, as demonstrated by a stagnant median ROE of 0% over a 10-year period [E26] and a persistent 1% ROE over shorter 3-year [E28] and 5-year [E27] horizons. The company's fundamental inefficiency is further underscored by a meager ROA of 0.91% compared to a sector benchmark of 2.86% [E8] and an overall ROE of 0.66% against a sector benchmark of 4.99% [E9], confirming that management deploys capital far less effectively than industry peers. Furthermore, investors receive zero income protection while paying this steep price, as the dividend yield sits entirely at 0.00% [E4]. Conceded: the company has expanded its TTM operating margin to 41% from 35% three years earlier [E30].

The bear focuses heavily on the extreme valuation multiples such as the P/E ratio of 929x [E1] and 934.06x against the sector benchmark [E6], alongside a price-to-book of 8.47x [E2], but these multiples completely overlook the impressive margin expansion underway where operating margins reached 41% in TTM compared to 35% three years earlier [E30]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], the ROA is 0.91% against a sector benchmark of 2.86% [E8], and the ROE sits at 0.66% against a sector benchmark of 4.99% [E9]. Conceded: the median return on equity is 0% over 10 years [E26], and sits at 1% over 5-year [E27], 3-year [E28], and last year horizons [E29], with a low 3-year ROE flag of 0.58% [E53]. However, the bear's emphasis on historical low returns ignores the positive trajectory of operational efficiency shown by the 6 percentage point improvement in operating margin over three years [E30].

The bull attempts to downplay extreme valuation multiples—such as the P/E of 929x [E1], 934.06x versus the 18.13x sector benchmark [E6], and a price-to-book of 8.47x [E2] against a 1.42x sector benchmark [E7]—by pointing to a 6 percentage point operating margin expansion to 41% in TTM [E30]. However, this single margin metric cannot justify a valuation trading at roughly 51 times the sector's P/E benchmark, especially when quarterly operating margins have actually slipped to 12% in Jun 2026 compared to 13% a year prior [E31]. Conceded: operating margins expanded over the three-year TTM window [E30]. Yet, this slight operational improvement fails to offset a dreadful multi-year return profile that the bull concedes, including a 10-year median ROE of 0% [E26] and a 3-year median ROE flagging low at 0.58% [E53]. Paying a massive premium for a business generating a meager 0.66% ROE [E9]—which dramatically trails the 4.99% sector benchmark [E9] and 0.91% ROA [E8]—represents an unsupportable disconnect between price and fundamental wealth creation.
